criteria_quotes: Lumbar spinal fusion may be considered medically necessary in individuals with any of the following conditions:
A. Spinal fracture with instability or neural compression; or

B. Spinal repair surgery for dislocation, tumor, or infection (including abscess, osteomyelitis, discitis, or fungal infection) when debridement is necessary and the extent of the debridement to help eradicate the infection creates or could create an unstable spine; or

C. Spinal stenosis when all of the following Criteria are met:
1. Neurogenic claudication or radicular pain; and
2. Documented central, lateral recess, or foraminal stenosis, with or without disc protrusion/herniation, facet arthropathy or facet cyst, or ligamentum flavum hypertrophy on MRI or other advanced imaging consistent with the individual’s symptoms; and
3. Spondylolisthesis at a level (L1-S1) to be included in the fusion demonstrated on x-rays, CT, or MRI or there is a high likelihood of post-operative instability due to severity of stenosis and extent of decompression/facetectomy as evidenced with findings including but not limited to disruption of the posterior elements due to facet joint excision that exceeds 50% bilaterally or 75% or more of a single facet during spinal decompression, removal of the pars interarticularis that requires fusion to stabilize, or complete or partial corpectomy; and
4. There is either clinical documentation of significant functional impairment or disability, or objective measurement of severe disability using the Oswestry Disability Index tool; and
5. There is clinical documentation that a minimum of three months of conservative nonoperative therapy failed to adequately treat the individual’s current symptoms including one or more of the following:
a. Documented cauda equina syndrome, progressive motor loss, or subjective worsening of symptoms during a course of conservative management when clearly documented in the medical record; or
b. All of the following Criteria are met:
i. Physical therapy or professionally-directed therapeutic independent home exercise program unless contraindication is clearly documented; and
ii. Two or more of the following treatment modalities have been attempted:
a.) Prescription anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics, or prescription strength doses of OTC anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; or
b.) Adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants; or
c.) Alternative therapies such as, but not limited to acupuncture, chiropractic manipulation, massage therapy, yoga, meditation; or
d.) Injection therapy of epidural or facet joint implicated pain sources in the area of concern, including but not limited to epidural steroid injection, medial branch block, radiofrequency ablation, selective nerve root injection, or discogram; and
6. The individual is nicotine-free OR there is clinical documentation that the individual has been abstinent from nicotine use for at least six weeks prior to planned procedure based on attestation or laboratory results (cotinine or nicotine levels); or
D. Single- or multi-session (staged) fusion for severe, progressive idiopathic scoliosis (i.e., lumbar or thoracolumbar) with Cobb angle greater than 40 degrees; or
E. Single- or multi-session (staged) fusion for severe degenerative scoliosis or severe spinal deformities when all of the following Criteria are met...

F. Isthmic spondylolisthesis when all of the following Criteria are met:
1. Either congenital (Wiltse type I) or acquired pars defect (Wiltse II), documented on x-ray; and
2. Persistent (daily) back pain, with or without neurogenic claudication or radicular pain; and
3. There is either clinical documentation of significant functional impairment or disability, or objective measurement of severe disability using the Oswestry Disability Index tool; and
4. There is clinical documentation that a minimum of three months of conservative nonoperative therapy failed to adequately treat the individual’s current symptoms including one or more of the following [same as C.5 above]...
5. The individual is nicotine-free OR there is clinical documentation that the individual has been abstinent from nicotine use for at least six weeks prior to planned procedure...

G. Recurrent same level central, foraminal, or lateral recess stenosis, or recurrent same level, disc herniation when all of the following Criteria are met:
1. Previous surgery was performed at least six months ago and resulted in significant interval relief of prior primary symptoms unless there is documented cauda equina syndrome, progressive motor loss, or subjective worsening of symptoms in the medical records; and
2. Recent imaging consistent with signs and symptoms associated with either of the following;
a. Recurrent same level central, foraminal, or lateral recess stenosis; or
b. Evidence of recurrent same level, disc herniation with neurogenic claudication or radicular pain including but not limited to dynamic segmental instability on flexion-extension plain x-rays, comparison of a supine and upright image with a difference in translational alignment between vertebrae great than 3mm between views, and Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis; and
3. There is either clinical documentation of significant functional impairment or disability, or objective measurement of severe disability using the Oswestry Disability Index tool;
4. There is clinical documentation that a minimum of three months of conservative nonoperative therapy failed to adequately treat... [and]
5. The individual is nicotine-free or abstinent from nicotine use for at least six weeks...

H. Adjacent segment degeneration when all of the following Criteria are met:
1. Previous surgery was performed at least 12 months ago and resulted in significant interval relief of prior primary symptoms... [and]
2. Central, foraminal, or lateral recess stenosis, with or without disc protrusion/herniation, facet arthropathy or facet cyst, or ligamentum flavum hypertrophy with neurogenic claudication or radicular pain documented by recent imaging consistent with signs and symptoms; and
3. There is either clinical documentation of significant functional impairment or disability, or objective measurement of severe disability using the Oswestry Disability Index tool

The appeal can be submitted using the Regence Member Appeal Form (FORM 4581WA) through the following routes depending on plan type:

For Commercial and Individual members:
- Mail: Attn: Regence Level 1 Member Appeals, Regence BlueShield, PO Box 1106, Lewiston, ID 83501-1106
- Fax: 1 (877) 663-7526
- Email: MemberAppeals@regence.com

For Self-Funded Groups (ASO) members:
- Mail: Attn: ASO Member Appeals, Regence BlueShield, PO Box 1106, Lewiston, ID 83501-1106
- Fax: 1 (888) 496-1542
- Email: MemberAppeals@regence.com
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The policy is publicly available online at http://blue.regence.com/trgmedpol/surgery/sur187.pdf. Alternatively, the patient can request the criteria applied to their case by calling Regence BlueShield Customer Service using the phone number printed on the back of their member ID card.
answer.notes: The governing medical policy (SUR187) is in effect for dates of service starting July 1, 2026, which matches the timing of this August 2026 denial. The clinical reason for the denial is 'incomplete documentation.' The patient's provider should submit clinical documents satisfying all elements of the specific category above (e.g., MRI/imaging reports, documentation of 3+ months of failed conservative therapy including physical therapy, and confirmation of nicotine-free status) alongside the completed Regence Appeal Form (FORM 4581WA).

Member: Emerson Delgado
Member ID: W727121486
Plan: Regence BlueShield (Commercial/ACA), state of Washington

Dear Emerson,

We reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider for the following service:

    Requested service: Lower back (lumbar) fusion
    Procedure code (CPT): 22612

After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-02-03).

Reference number: POC-A93FE7E3B5-95850

1. Neurogenic claudication or radicular pain; and
2. Documented central, lateral recess, or foraminal stenosis, with or without disc protrusion/herniation, facet arthropathy or facet cyst, or ligamentum flavum hypertrophy on MRI or other advanced imaging consistent with the individual’s symptoms; and
3. 5. There is clinical documentation that a minimum of three months of conservative nonoperative therapy failed to adequately treat the individual’s current symptoms including one or more of the following:
a. Documented cauda equina syndrome, progressive motor loss, or subjective worsening of symptoms during a course of conservative management when clearly documented in the medical record; or
b. All of the following Criteria are met:
i. Physical therapy or professionally-directed therapeutic independent home exercise program unless contraindication is clearly documented; and
ii. Two or more of the following treatment modalities have been attempted:
a.) Prescription anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics, or prescription strength doses of OTC anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; or
b.) Adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants; or
c.) Alternative therapies such as, but not limited to acupuncture, chiropractic manipulation, massage therapy, yoga, meditation; or
